absent: Full layouts and locking of mm_walk, vm_area_struct, hmm_range, hmm_dma_map and mmu_interval_notifier beyond fields touched here.
Behaviour of the generic page table iterator, hugetlb address resolution, huge state helpers, and the locked HMM fault engine.
Detailed callback contracts and error values for pre and post hooks, hugetlb entry and hole handling beyond abort on nonzero.
Numeric order constants, transparent huge page flag bit positions, and shared memory mount control values.
Device IOVA reservation, peer to peer classification, and physical DMA mapping internals.

findings.text: Page walk test hook decides whether an address interval should be entered. If the operations vector supplies a custom test callback it fully determines the outcome. Otherwise a PFNMAP mapping is treated as having no ordinary page backing: when a hole callback exists it handles the whole interval and a skip is signalled, while without a hole callback the interval is skipped silently. Normal mappings return a proceed indication.

Range walk entry rejects installation requests on hugetlb mappings. It runs an optional pre hook that can abort, then dispatches hugetlb mappings to a hugetlb iterator when a hugetlb callback is present and all other mappings to the generic page table iterator, and finally runs an optional post hook before reporting the accumulated status.

Hugetlb iteration is clamped so each step covers at most one huge page. The chunk end is the smaller of the caller supplied range end and the end of the huge page containing the current address, derived from that size class mask and size.

Enabled hugetlb walk holds the mapping read lock for the whole range and advances chunk by chunk. Each chunk resolves its page table entry under the huge page aligned address; a present entry is delivered to the hugetlb callback, a missing entry is delivered to the hole callback when one exists, and any reported error stops the scan and is returned.
One build configuration provides a hugetlb range walker that performs no work and reports success unconditionally, indicating hugetlb iteration is disabled there.

Walk locking helpers distinguish address space and per mapping modes. Address space read mode asserts read ownership and other modes except a per mapping verify mode assert write ownership. Per mapping handling acquires write ownership in write mode and only asserts the expected read or write ownership in verify modes, with read mode delegated to the address space helper and everything compiled out when per mapping locks are unavailable.

Interval read start samples the subscription generation under a spin lock and notes whether an invalidation is in progress by equality with the global generation. It records lock dependency markers, sleeps until the global generation moves when caught inside an invalidation, and returns the sampled generation without looping, leaving retry detection to a later check so callers can bound total time.
Synchronous heterogeneous memory range fault is a thin wrapper that invokes the locked fault engine with no lock tracking argument.

Unlocked fault with timeout repeatedly starts a notifier sequence, takes the address space read lock in killable mode, rejects unstable address spaces, enforces an optional deadline, then calls the locked fault engine while tracking whether the engine dropped the lock. It releases the lock only when still held and retries only on busy status, restarting the deadline when the previous attempt had dropped the lock.

Device address mapping allocation refuses devices needing synchronous DMA handling or with limited addressing. On acceptance it records the per entry size, allocates a page frame number list, attempts to reserve contiguous device address space, allocates a device address list only when the platform requires explicit unmapping without such space, and frees the first list if the second allocation fails.
Mapping teardown releases reserved device address space when in use and frees both the page frame and device address lists.

Per page device mapping first handles pages already marked mapped by returning the existing address for reserved space or the stored address when unmapping is required, otherwise falling through to stateless regeneration. It then classifies peer state, marking host bridge traffic accordingly, returning a bus address directly for bus routed pages, and failing on unknown states. Reserved space uses link plus sync with unlink on sync failure, while the direct path maps physical memory and records the result when unmapping is required, marking success and clearing peer state on failure.

Per page unmap acts only when both valid and mapped marks are present, otherwise reporting no work. Bus routed peer pages need no unmap call, reserved space is detached, and direct mappings are unmapped only when the platform requires it, after which all mapping related marks are cleared and success is reported.

Observed page walk context carries a current mapping and an operations vector. The vector may supply test, hole, install, pre mapping, post mapping and hugetlb entry hooks, and hugetlb delivery receives the resolved entry, mask and chunk bounds together with the walk context.
The unset value for the shared huge zero page frame number is the all ones unsigned long, used to recognise that no persistent zero folio has been installed.

Default transparent huge page behaviour enables defragmentation requests for advised mappings and for the background collapse daemon plus use of the zero page, with additional always or advised mode bits selected by build configuration.

Deferred split tracking uses a dedicated lock class, a least recently used list and a shrinker pointer, while the shared huge zero folio is guarded by a spin lock with a separate atomic reference count and its own shrinker pointer.
File transparent huge page support requires an attached file whose inode is not an anonymous file, whose mapping advertises middle directory folio support, and whose mode is regular.

File huge page tunables are bypassed for forced collapse and for huge PFN mappings with a huge fault handler. Otherwise allowance follows global policy: always mode allows, advised global mode allows only mappings marked huge, and the combined check passes when either bypass or allowance holds.

File mapping eligibility first applies the tunables check, then trusts huge fault handlers in the fault path, accepts either huge fault handlers or enabled regular files for status reporting, and requires an enabled regular file on other paths. Allowable orders start from the intersection of requested and class specific supported orders for anonymous, special or direct access, and default file mappings, and are rejected for descriptorless mappings, hardware disabled or mapping disabled states, direct access mappings outside faults, and background collapse when the mapping opts out.

Outside the fault path unsuitable orders are pruned from the top down by testing size and alignment against the tail of the mapping. Shared memory mappings then intersect with inode policy, non anonymous mappings defer to file eligibility, temporary stacks are rejected, mappings without an anonymous structure are allowed only for status or fault paths, and remaining anonymous mappings keep the surviving orders.

Shared memory allowable orders are denied on hardware or mapping disable. Allocation without a mapping, non anonymous shared mappings, or forced huge mode return the global decision directly. Otherwise a top level deny forces zero, a top level force returns the inherit set, and the normal path unions the always set with within size and advised sets as applicable plus the inherit set when globally enabled, masked to default file orders.

Global shared memory enablement requires a regular inode, honours deny and force, grants all default orders for always mounts, grants the within size subset when non empty for within size mounts, grants all default orders for advised mounts marked huge, and otherwise denies. Within size computation scans candidate orders from largest down and keeps the remaining set once the rounded file size covers the aligned index, else yields none.
One configuration disables shared memory global huge page enablement entirely by returning no orders unconditionally.
Anonymous shared memory is recognised by identity of the mapping operations vector, and the shared memory superblock state is obtained from the generic filesystem private pointer.

Boot initialisation for the shared huge zero folio attempts allocation once, warning on failure and otherwise publishing its frame number and accounting an allocation event, while the matching shrinker exit and the memory release helper are empty in this configuration.

Callers interested in holes must supply a hole callback or PFNMAP intervals are silently skipped, and hugetlb installation requests fail rather than being partially applied. Device mapping callers must handle a mapping error sentinel on peer classification failure, link or sync failure, or physical map failure, and must not assume the device address list exists when the platform needs no explicit unmap.
This translation unit prefixes log messages with its module name, enables trace point definitions, and defaults to splitting underused transparent huge pages.
Anonymous transparent huge page order policy is held in three mostly read globals for always, advised and inherit modes with a boot time flag recording whether the administrator configured them.
